legend: The bone marrow aspirate smear (Wright–Giemsa) contains a spectrum of neoplastic cells including small, mature-appearing lymphocytes with scant cytoplasm (arrowheads) and plasma cells with prominent cytoplasmic vacuoles (arrow); background bone marrow elements (erythroid and myeloid precursors) are also present (<<30298>>). In this case of mu heavy chain disease, the aspirate smear (MGG) shows plasma cells with eccentric nuclei, clumped chromatin, and prominent cytoplasmic vacuoles, including some with multiple vacuoles (<<30998>>) and others with large single vacuoles (<<30999>>). Background small lymphocytes and normal maturing myeloid and erythroid elements are also present.
source: Robert McKenna, MD, Professor Emeritus, Department of Laboratory Medicine and Pathology, mcken138@umn.edu
